Unresolved is the finding: the strong form has no direct evidence and no direct disconfirmation.

treatment.plainLanguage: Held tension in blood-vessel walls is a kind of memory the mind uses — the grasping Buddhism calls clinging has a vascular implementation.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: No admitted record discriminates this from ordinary neurovascular physiology; the read path exists (VASO-C012) but instantaneous modulation is not storage.
treatment.strongestObjection: Hysteresis is not memory. A thermostat depends on its history and stores no autobiography; nothing shows a vascular state encodes content, persists after its cause, and biases later computation in an input-specific way.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An animal preparation in which different induced vascular states produce reliably different later neural responses under identical stimulation with oxygenation clamped (VASO-R005).
Information-theoretic evidence that vascular state predicts future neural state beyond what current neural and metabolic state predict.
A clean negative — vascular manipulation affecting neural gain only through instantaneous perfusion — would collapse the claim to weak vasocomputation.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The thesis is stated by its proponents (VASO-E013, VASO-E037) and undermined where it names a compartment: pressurized skeletal-muscle arterioles show maintained or rising phosphorylation, not the latch signature (VASO-E020); no arteriole energetic cost has ever been measured (VASO-E019); the critical report finds no study identifying a latch at a tender point and no time-resolved release (VASO-E016). The Doppler pattern near trigger points is compatible with contracture compression as much as distal constriction by the imaging authors' own account (VASO-E027, weighed at zero diagnosticity). The second essay's relocation to perforators (VASO-E044, VASO-E045) rests on an unread source and is treated as absent. Neither direction holds decisive evidence; the balance of what exists leans against the intramuscular latch form.

treatment.plainLanguage: A knot is a small blood vessel inside the muscle clamped shut by smooth muscle in its cheap latch, starving the tissue around it — a maintained state, not damaged tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis against which the perforator and guarding accounts compete; its distinctive predictions (cold on PET, blood before stiffness, breath-gated release) are unmeasured.
treatment.strongestObjection: Where the arteriole has been examined with the right molecular readout it shows sustained activation, not an economical hold; and the only imaged within-session disappearance of a trigger point came from pressure alone with breathing uninstructed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A pressurized skeletal-muscle arteriole holding constriction after stimulus withdrawal at falling phosphorylation with measured low energetic cost (VASO-R004).
Time-locked imaging showing perfusion rising before stiffness falls at a felt release, exceeding sham and pressure-only controls (VASO-R001).
A stiff, electrically active knot that is metabolically cold on FDG-PET (VASO-R013).
Against it: equal clearance under held breath, a hot knot on PET, or the non-latching motor-protein phenotype throughout skeletal-muscle arterioles.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Anchor-only: the claim is held on its statement in the proponent's second essay (SRC-JHONG-2026A), a source the ledger has not read and verified, with no admitted evidence record. The published works the essay invokes for the collar, the tether and the perforator anatomy are catalogued as its propositions, not retrieved. Featured because it is a genuinely different mechanism with cheap tests, not because anything supports it.

treatment.plainLanguage: On the perforator picture a knot is held by three things at once — the vessel's tone, a collar of gelled hyaluronan around the bundle, and the tether that collar makes between fascia and the tissue beneath — rather than by one latch.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If true it relocates the vascular element to the skin, drops the latch as a requirement, and absorbs pressure-alone release; it predicts perforator coincidence, breath gating by inspiratory reflex, and release by hydrodissection.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing has been measured. The one instrumented fact about knots — graded stiff regions blinded sonographers measure — lies inside the muscle, not in the fascia under the skin.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded tender points coinciding with pencil-Doppler perforators above chance (VASO-R015).
A knot released by saline hydrodissection at its perforator with no breath and no pressure (VASO-R017).
A local skin-perfusion flash time-locked to the exhale and the felt star, absent at sham sites and blocked by inhale-and-hold (VASO-R016).
Against it: tender points on perforators no more often than chance.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One record in either direction: the founding essay's uncited assertion that the traditional maps cluster the important knots along the torso midline and limbs (VASO-E039, weak), with no coding rule and no chance baseline. No blinded anatomical coding exists; every apparent convergence is vulnerable to post-hoc matching.

treatment.plainLanguage: The Tibetan channel-knots, Hindu granthis and Chinese ashi points are maps of the same tension system, drawn from the inside by practitioners with trained body awareness.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Even a genuine alignment with vascular geography would show that the traditions located something real, not that anything latches or clenches; it does not decide among the three accounts.
treatment.strongestObjection: Correspondence found after the fact is the weakest kind of evidence, and the maps could align with nerves, fascia or bony landmarks as well as vessels.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Preregistered coding of rtsa mdud, granthi and ashi locations into a common coordinate system aligning with perforators, sympathetic chains or dorsal root ganglia above chance (VASO-R006).
A null under the same design would retire the convergence argument.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The latch-bridge model is textbook smooth-muscle physiology (VASO-E003, strong): dephosphorylated cross-bridges detach slowly, sustaining stress at low activation. The study table qualifies its generality — latch behaviour present in the rabbit femoral artery and absent one branch order downstream, never followed further (VASO-E021) — and the essay's restatement (VASO-E034) overstates it as zero activation. The capability is real; its presence in the vessels a knot would need is a separate, untested question.

treatment.plainLanguage: Smooth muscle in vessel walls can lock and hold tension for almost nothing after the signal that made it contract fades.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Conventional physiology predicts it too; that the latch exists in conduit arteries decides nothing about tender points.
treatment.strongestObjection: Latch behaviour is not generic across vascular smooth muscle and has never been measured in an arteriole of any bed.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A paired-caliber study finding latch capacity persisting or disappearing down the arteriolar tree of skeletal muscle (VASO-R004).
Retrieved energetic measurements in resistance vessels.

claimAssessments.reasoning: A conditional inference graded on physiological priors, stated as such: tissue remodeling takes days to weeks, so a change completing in seconds is a change of maintained state. The essay states the argument (VASO-E035, weak); the imaged changes the ledger holds moved over visits after needling (VASO-E030, context). Its premise — that the felt release corresponds to an objective local event within seconds — has never been measured; the nearest instrumented disappearance of a trigger point, held on VASO-C005, ran over minutes of compression.

treatment.plainLanguage: If a knot really lets go in seconds, whatever let go was something the body was doing, not scar tissue.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Decides state against scar but not vascular against guarding or densification — all three are states.
treatment.strongestObjection: The antecedent is unverified; and 'state' includes sustained motor guarding and fascial densification, neither of which needs a vessel.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-resolved elastography and Doppler showing a local transition within seconds of an exhale (VASO-R001).
Felt releases without reproducible local transitions would remove the premise.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Anchor-only: held on the founding essay's statement that fascial densification is reversible with pressure, movement and warmth, with no admitted evidence record; the Stecco-group primaries remain blocked and the reversal timescale unretrieved.

treatment.plainLanguage: The thickened, gluey lubricant between fascial layers can be thinned again by pressure, movement and warmth.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If densification reverses within a session under pressure, the knot can be a state without being a vessel and pressure alone should work — a direct non-vascular competitor.
treatment.strongestObjection: No retrieved study reports the timescale; the concept rests on anatomical and mechanistic work, not on prospective demonstration at a painful point.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrieved primaries reporting hyaluronan viscosity or fascial glide reversing under load and warmth, with timescale (VASO-R008).
Stiffness dropping at a release with no perfusion change would favour this account.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Proposed as a hypothesis in 2008 (VASO-E004, context) and given a demonstrated mechanism in 2024: blood-pressure pulsations modulate central neurons through mechanosensitive channels in rat preparations and awake animals (VASO-E005, strong). Provisional because it is rat brain, not human periphery, and instantaneous modulation, not storage.

treatment.plainLanguage: The state of local blood vessels can change what nearby nerve cells do — blood talks back.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows vessels can nudge neurons now, not that they store anything; conventional neurovascular biology accommodates it.
treatment.strongestObjection: The extension from rat brain to peripheral sensory endings beside vessels is argument, not measurement.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Peripheral demonstration of vessel-caliber-to-afferent modulation.
History dependence beyond instantaneous perfusion (VASO-R005).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review documents reproducible rises in heart-rate variability and respiratory sinus arrhythmia under slow breathing in healthy humans (VASO-E009, strong); the essay's restatement adds nothing (VASO-E036). The evidence establishes a global shift measured on the heart, in people with no tender point in the study.

treatment.plainLanguage: Breathing slowly, especially with long exhales, reliably tilts the nervous system toward its rest-and-digest side.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A global shift that every account accepts; the local site-specific effect the thesis adds is unmeasured.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing here reaches a tender point; the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate skin or skeletal-muscle vessels.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Local tissue measurement during slow breathing at a palpated site.
Breath-randomised compression showing gating or its absence (VASO-R020).

claimAssessments.reasoning: A systematic review finds manual examination not shown to be reliable or valid, with no reference standard (VASO-E011, strong); the principal critique argues the construct is circular (VASO-E010, moderate); the imaging authors concede examiner dependence (VASO-E029) and the runners' group states there is no gold standard and palpation variability cannot be trained away (VASO-E078, VASO-E079), with imaging confirming 71.5% of palpated spots (VASO-E081; VASO-E080 context).

treatment.plainLanguage: Examiners do not reliably agree on where trigger points are, there is no agreed standard for what one is, and whether the construct is real is disputed in the literature.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Caps every observation in the case: whatever is measured was located by an unproven method; a quarter of palpated spots may be something else.
treatment.strongestObjection: Imaging-anchored localization may escape the problem, and blinded sonographers do find graded stiffness at palpated sites.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Demonstrated inter-examiner reliability against an instrumented reference.
A census with blinded palpation and imaging showing high concordance (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Croft 1994 supplies the first population record: two people reporting no pain had eleven or more tender points (VASO-E082, weak) in a pain-selected sample (VASO-E083, context). The essay's ubiquity claims (VASO-E015) and the imaging introduction's prevalence figure (VASO-E028) are second-hand and weak; the critical report qualifies that the spots' very existence is part of the debate (VASO-E012); the scanner record is feasibility context only (VASO-E018).

treatment.plainLanguage: Small, sharply tender spots in muscle are common in ordinary people, not only in patients.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: That tender points are common decides nothing about what they are.
treatment.strongestObjection: No census exists; the one survey is pain-selected and tests fixed sites, not palpable knots.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Retrieval of unselected community surveys with count distributions (VASO-R010).
The knot census with pain-free controls, children and meditators (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Hubbard & Berkoff recorded sustained activity in the nidus of every trigger point and none at adjacent non-tender sites (VASO-E001, moderate); Simons 2002 qualifies exclusivity — endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites and none off the zone (VASO-E031) — so the claim as stated (a prevalence gradient) is what the two together support. The essay's restatement (VASO-E043) and the equine cross-species note (VASO-E052, unread source) add no weight.

treatment.plainLanguage: Trigger points hum electrically at a millimeter scale more often than nearby non-tender sites in the same nerve-supply zone, and never where there is no such zone.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A localized maintained signature any account must explain, but it is skeletal-endplate electrophysiology and fits guarding as well as a vascular write.
treatment.strongestObjection: The signature tracks the endplate zone first; the silent controls of 1993 may simply have lain off it.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Repeat with a matched endplate-zone control (VASO-R011).
Retrieved phentolamine or relaxation primaries quieting the nidus (VASO-R009, VASO-R012).

claimAssessments.reasoning: One primary (VASO-E002, moderate): mental arithmetic raised activity at trigger points while control sites in the same muscle stayed comparatively quiet, without tensing, in fourteen subjects. Never replicated; no vascular measure. The essay's restatement (VASO-E033) is zero weight. Read beside VASO-E031 on the parent claim, the control site was not matched to the endplate zone — a disclosed cross-claim basis for holding the localization open.

treatment.plainLanguage: Giving someone a math test turns up the electrical activity inside a tender point but not a centimeter away — the brain has the knot's address.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Shows a mental event writes to a discrete site; three readings — stress-sensitive endplates, an arteriolar write, a skin-territory write — fit it equally.
treatment.strongestObjection: The control needle may have sat off the endplate zone, so the stressor may raise any endplate-zone site.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Trigger point rising while a matched endplate-zone control does not (VASO-R011).
A skin-perfusion fall over the point and not control skin during arithmetic.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Anchor-only: held on the proponent's second essay (SRC-JHONG-2026A), a source the ledger has not read, with no admitted evidence record. The reading — the stressor's site-selective rise as a regional sympathetic vasoconstriction written to skin — is stated, not observed.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stress response at a knot is the body blushing or blanching in one small patch of skin — a sympathetic signal aimed at a skin territory.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would explain addressability without the brain targeting a millimeter of muscle; separates the perforator account from guarding if a local skin-perfusion fall is found.
treatment.strongestObjection: The recorded signal is skeletal-muscle electrophysiology inside the muscle, not skin perfusion.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Laser speckle over the point during mental arithmetic showing a localized perfusion fall not present over control skin (VASO-R016).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported only by first-person testimony from the hypothesis's proponent (VASO-E014, weak), in an essay whose text was AI-generated at the author's direction; consistent with practitioner lore, contradicted by no one, measured by no one. Real evidence that people feel a release; no evidence that anything happens in the tissue within seconds.

treatment.plainLanguage: Press on a knot, breathe out slowly, and within seconds something feels like it lets go.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The anchor observation of the case; as testimony it cannot separate an objective local event from expectation riding on global relaxation.
treatment.strongestObjection: Expectation and attention produce felt releases without local change; nothing time-resolved has been recorded.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Time-locked stiffness and perfusion transitions at a felt release exceeding sham and pressure-only controls (VASO-R001).
Felt releases without reproducible local transitions would reduce it to a percept.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its anchor in the founding essay with one admitted record, in direction context (VASO-E067): a published pressure-only protocol carried no breathing instruction, recording or manipulation anywhere in its methods or results — and nothing more. The outcome of that protocol is admitted on VASO-C005 (VASO-E072), over a course of up to three thirty-second compressions, and is not spent as a grade here. Breathing was uncontrolled, the endpoint was sonographic disappearance over minutes rather than a felt release in seconds, and the outcome records proposed on this claim were refused as bundled. Neither supported nor contradicted on its own records.

treatment.plainLanguage: Pressing on a knot without working the breath does not release it — both keys are needed.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Decides whether the breath is a key at all, and with it the cleanest argument that the releasing element answers to autonomic state.
treatment.strongestObjection: A pressure-only protocol with nobody told how to breathe made most imaged trigger points undetectable within a session — though uninstructed breathing is not held breath.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Pressure during inhale-and-hold clearing points no less than free breathing — breath not a key (VASO-R020).
Inhale-and-hold blocking clearance while slow exhalation matches or beats free breathing — breath gating.
Release by hydrodissection with no breath (VASO-R017).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Anchor-only: stated as a prediction in the founding essay with no admitted evidence record. No time-resolved Doppler and elastography have been acquired at a release; the runners' study performed no Doppler and archived no cine loops, so the order of blood and stiffness change was not observed.

treatment.plainLanguage: When a knot releases with the breath, blood flow returns first and the tissue softens second.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The one timing prediction both vascular accounts make and neither guarding nor densification makes; falsifiable and cheap.
treatment.strongestObjection: Nothing has been filmed; stiffness leading or simultaneous change would favour the non-vascular accounts.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Perfusion rise leading stiffness drop across release events (VASO-R001, VASO-R016).
Stiffness leading, or the two simultaneous, would falsify it.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Supported by microdialysis (VASO-E006), the imaging review as characterized second-hand (VASO-E007), and Ballyns 2011's blinded stiffness gradient (VASO-E023) and group-level Doppler difference (VASO-E022); qualified by the same source's no-pain-free-controls limitation (VASO-E026) and non-classifying indices (VASO-E025), and by Landfald's active-versus-latent comparison having no control tissue (VASO-E070). Landfald's pain, stiffness-ratio and first-round disappearance figures are context (VASO-E068, VASO-E069, VASO-E071, VASO-E072). Essay restatements (VASO-E042, VASO-E050, VASO-E051) carry no weight. Measurable differences exist; the vascular component is partial.

treatment.plainLanguage: Active trigger points measurably differ from surrounding tissue — more acidic, stiffer, with somewhat different blood flow nearby.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Every account predicts local differences; compression by contracted fiber produces them as readily as a throttled vessel.
treatment.strongestObjection: Comparisons sit inside symptomatic muscle; mediators were elevated at remote sites too; one Doppler index shows no difference.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A Doppler and elastography census with pain-free controls (VASO-R002).
Perfusion measured in the muscle bed itself, not conduit-scale waveforms.

claimAssessments.reasoning: One preregistered within-subject study in 57 volunteers (VASO-E008, strong): attention toward the histamine site produced ~1.5-fold smaller, faster-resolving responses in ~90% of participants with no arousal difference and higher HRV. Provisional because single-lab and very recent; qualified by the route being vagal immune regulation over tens of minutes in a tissue the parasympathetic system does not directly innervate (VASO-E041).

treatment.plainLanguage: Simply paying attention to an inflamed spot makes the inflammation smaller and shorter, without any change in stress arousal.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: An existence proof that cognition can regulate a peripheral vascular bed at a chosen site; it says nothing about knots, smooth muscle or seconds.
treatment.strongestObjection: The demonstrated route is vagal immune regulation over minutes, not vascular grip or release.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication.
An analogous attention manipulation at a palpated tender point with local stiffness and perfusion endpoints.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports a median pulsatility index of 8.3 near active sites against 3.0 near normal sites (VASO-E022, moderate); qualified by the absence of a pain-free control group (VASO-E026). Vessels interrogated were conduit-scale, 1–2 cm from the point.

treatment.plainLanguage: Arteries near active trigger points show flow that surges and falls more sharply with each heartbeat than arteries near normal sites in the same muscle.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Consistent with something downstream resisting flow, whether a clenched vessel or contracted fiber compressing the bed; the index could not classify individual sites.
treatment.strongestObjection: High variance, no pain-free controls, and the authors list contracture and transducer pressure as candidate causes.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Replication with pain-free controls and microvascular Doppler (VASO-R002).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 reports retrograde diastolic flow at 15 of 49 palpably normal sites, 31% (VASO-E022, moderate), with the caveat that these sites lie in symptomatic muscle (VASO-E026).

treatment.plainLanguage: Blood flowing backward between heartbeats shows up near about a third of palpably normal spots in muscles that have trigger points elsewhere.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Turns the waveform into a gradient across symptomatic muscle rather than a marker of a knot; mildly against any marker reading.
treatment.strongestObjection: Could be spillover from neighbouring points or true baseline; the study cannot say which.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Baseline retrograde-flow rates in pain-free subjects.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 gives blinded-sonographer stiff areas of 0.57, 0.36 and 0.17 cm² at active, latent and normal sites, separating classes with AUC 0.8–0.9 (VASO-E023, moderate). Landfald 2025's calf findings are a parallel from another muscle and method, held as context (VASO-E074, VASO-E076, VASO-E077); the compound record VASO-E073 is not spent. Sites were selected by palpation, so the contrast presupposes the classification.

treatment.plainLanguage: The stiff region around a trigger point is bigger at active points than latent ones, and bigger at latent ones than at normal sites.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Real graded stiffness inside the muscle; says nothing about what the stiff tissue is, and sits in the muscle rather than the fascia the perforator account names.
treatment.strongestObjection: Single vibration frequency, palpation-selected sites, same NIH lineage as the biochemistry.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Shear-wave replication by an independent group with blinded site selection.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons 2002 abstract: endplate noise at four of eleven non-tender endplate-zone sites outside trigger points, P = 0.024 (VASO-E032, moderate). Abstract only; nonrandomized and unblinded by the authors' own description; ten subjects.

treatment.plainLanguage: The faint electrical hum found at trigger points also turns up at some non-tender spots in the nerve-supply zone, just less often.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Undercuts the exclusivity reading of the nidus and favours the endplate-zone interpretation.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded, abstract-only, from proponents of the construct.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded replication with per-site amplitudes (VASO-R011).

claimAssessments.reasoning: Simons 2002 abstract: endplate noise did not occur at taut-band sites outside an endplate zone, P = 0.000034 (VASO-E032, moderate). Same design limits as VASO-C034.

treatment.plainLanguage: Where there is no nerve-supply zone, a taut band produces no electrical hum.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Locates the signature in the endplate zone; a vascular account must explain why an electrical, skeletal marker tracks the endplate zone.
treatment.strongestObjection: Small, unblinded, abstract-only.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Blinded replication; any recording of spontaneous activity at an off-zone taut band.

claimAssessments.reasoning: Ballyns 2011 detected no differences in resistivity index between normal, latent and active sites (VASO-E024, moderate); a within-patient comparison in symptomatic subjects, which the authors partly attribute to proximity of normal sites to trigger points.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second measure of downstream blood-flow resistance shows no difference at all between trigger points and normal spots.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A negative that caps the vascular footprint: the signature at trigger points is partial, not categorical.
treatment.strongestObjection: No pain-free controls; normal sites may share the abnormality by proximity.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Resistivity differences appearing against pain-free control tissue.
